title: What is the smallest multiple of all the numbers from one to ten?
description: The smallest number for one to ten except seven was three hundred sixty. Seven now has to fit in as well, and testing the multiples of three hundred sixty finds the smallest number that works.
teaching_notes: One idea: the new number must be a multiple of the old answer, so test only its multiples. Watch for students who start again with all ten numbers.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q10, p.111 (Try This)
video_script.why: The child reuses the smallest number for all except seven, and tests its multiples until seven fits in too.
video_script.substitution: Test the multiples of the last answer one by one until the new number fits.
video_script.anchor: the numbers one to ten and the multiples of three hundred sixty written in a row
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest number is two thousand five hundred and twenty

final_answer.spoken: the smallest number is two thousand five hundred and twenty

maths_rules: from the last question the smallest multiple of all of 1 to 10 except 7 is 360, so the new number is a multiple of 360
video_script.design: One idea: the new number is a multiple of the old answer, so test its multiples for the missing number. Same method as the book example: common multiples are multiples of one number.
